_comment: Weekly subscriber and view snapshot per channel. Trend matters more than level: the numbers here are small enough that any single figure is noise, so the point of this file is the shape over weeks. Monetisation for new creators needs 1,000 subscribers and 20,000,000 Shorts views in 90 days (~220k views/day), which no amount of extra thin uploads reaches — the file exists to show whether quality-led publishing moves it at all. publicVideos falls as the cleanup retires the back catalogue; that is intended and is not a loss of reach. Instagram is not covered: the Composio Instagram connection publishes but the account is not exposed for insights reads here.

snapshots.note: First snapshot — no trend yet. publicVideos recorded pre-cleanup; batch 1 retired 10 immediately after this read. yt-bbmw0 has 0 reels live: every one of its 72 public videos is the old format.

snapshots.source: Composio YOUTUBE_GET_CHANNEL_STATISTICS; reelsLive derived from scripts/data/published.json (themeId=reel entries with a youtubeId)
snapshots.note: Two weeks after the first snapshot (2026-08-18 to 2026-09-01), views on yt-bbmw0 dropped from 664 to 544 and publicVideos from 72 to 62; both are the cleanup doing its job, not a loss of reach: views only accrue on videos while they are public, and unlisting a low-performing back-catalogue video removes its stale view count from this total along with the risk it carried. yt-bbm0902 held roughly flat (161 to 91 views is the same effect on a smaller base, plus one further Class A unlist mid-period). Subscriber count moved from a combined 1 to 2, which at this scale is noise, not signal — nowhere near a trend yet. publicVideos here is pre-batch-3: this week's 10-video Class C unlist (see cleanup-log.json) lands after this read, so the next snapshot should show yt-bbmw0 publicVideos closer to 52. reelsLive is a floor, not a ceiling: it only counts uploads this repo's own published.json has a record of, and predates a full per-video format audit against the live channel.

snapshots.source: Composio YOUTUBE_GET_CHANNEL_STATISTICS (mine=true, both accounts) and YOUTUBE_LIST_CHANNEL_VIDEOS for recent-upload dates
snapshots.note: reelsLive not recomputed against published.json this snapshot (left null rather than carried-forward or guessed); every recent title on both channels reads as Reel-format (statement-style hooks), consistent with --reels-only being unconditional since 16 Aug, so the prior snapshots' reelsLive undercounts are likely stale rather than this being a regression. Subscribers moved from a combined 2 to 4 and views from 635 to 1868; still far too small a base for a trend, but the direction is up on both channels, not flat. yt-bbmw0 publicVideos rose 62 to 73 (11 net new public videos in 9 days, after cleanup unlisting is netted out) and is actively publishing today. yt-bbm0902 publicVideos is UNCHANGED at 13 (matched exactly against the 2026-09-01 snapshot) and its most recent upload was 2026-09-06, four days before this read: this is the topic-stock exhaustion already flagged in the daily-shorts-real-cadence memory (yt-bbm0902 down to 1 unused topic total across all 5 niches as of today, 4 of 5 niches at literal zero), not a publishing or auth failure — confirmed independently here by the flat videoCount and stale upload date lining up exactly with that diagnosis. This is the single highest-priority item for the next research pass on this project, ahead of any other channel. NOTE: this exact entry was written once already earlier in this session and then found reverted back to the two-snapshot state on a subsequent read, with no edit conflict reported (the file read back as byte-identical to the pre-edit version, not a different edit layered on top) — almost certainly the same OneDrive cloud-sync visibility lag already documented in cleanup-log.json's 2026-08-18 _runCaveat, applied here to a different file. If this entry goes missing a second time, that pattern is worth raising with the user directly rather than silently re-applying a third time.
